I have the skill to build and improve on this hardware, but I have no farming skill. I'm currently trying and failing to grow flowers (my flower bed has already been reclaimed by the persistent nearby Ivy), I'm also trying to grow radishes with doubtfull results.

The biggest issue with this platform is that they use 3d printed plastics for outdoor use. Those will just melt on a sunny day. The thing will fail during summer because of this.

I agree that for cost/crop value this is totally not worth it. But for someone like me, I would build this just for the satisfaction of having a plant not die on me.
I feel the money would be better spent on a botany or gardening course rather than this bot if all you care about is your plants staying alive.

The software aspect and some of the sensors could be really useful, set up a soil sensor and the weed monitoring system that sends alerts to your phone so you know what's going on with it could be very useful. But mechanization aspect of it is simply too expensive for what it does, and it doesn't even harvest the crops so you're going to have to get into the dirt anyway, may as well plant and weed as well at that point.

Setting up a crop plan with the software and seeding it yourself, then letting the program keep track of it's estimated growth with a timer along with a soil sensor for quality management. That's about as far as I'd use it, and all of that can be done by hand so the whole package for $2,900 is simply too much money for not enough gain.

It might make your gardening slightly easier with reduced weeding, but outside of the software for ease of use I don't see much need of it.

I garden as a hobby. Because I want to, not because I need to. It feels good to grow something with nothing but my own sweat and labor. The most complicated piece of machinery I use is a rotary sprinkler with a timer. This would be a colossal investment, to basically save me the labor of weeding and planting. Which are labors i kind of enjoy. There's a sense of satisfaction i get from making the garden look nice. Now, if it also worked as a sentry turret and killed squirrels and groundhogs.
